A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable main text, equations, payoff matrices, Algorithm 1 and appendices A-C. Renumbering and layout changes do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v6 reports theoretical bounds, constructed game examples and proofs. Its applications and appendices contain no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v7 remains theoretical. The added tightness proposition and extended example are analytical results, not empirical measurements or simulations.

M1.justification: The agent construction in Appendix B.2 changes: v6 includes a fallback to a no-swap-regret learner if the principal deviates; v7 directly computes the prescribed history-dependent principal policy and approximately best responds, without that fallback. This procedural change is confined to the tightness construction; the central reduction and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation tasks. Bayesian persuasion, Stackelberg games and contract design remain the same theoretical application domains.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Additional related-work citations do not introduce experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to regret conditions and analytical constructions concern the theory, not training budgets, evaluation metrics or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, sensitivity tests or robustness analyses. The extended Bayesian persuasion example establishes mathematical tightness and is covered under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Expectations and regret bounds are mathematical quantities.

E6.justification: There are no empirical scores or measured findings in either version. The payoff matrices and mean-based exploitation example retain their numerical entries and conclusions; changes to symbolic utility bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Several central theoretical statements and arguments change. Definition 2.1 drops explicit quantification over every principal strategy. Theorem 3.3 becomes Proposition 3.3, excludes dependence on the agent's current strategy, changes the bound's regret argument from CReg(T)/(2T) to CReg(T)/T, and replaces Appendix B.2's proof. Theorem 3.4's proof corrects conditioning to include both signal and action and replaces v with u in the principal-utility calculation. New Proposition 3.5 asserts attainability of the maximax bound, with proof omitted; Example 4.1 and Appendix C.2 add the bound maximax OBJ^R(δ) ≥ U* + δ. These substantially revise the scope and support of the tightness results.

C1.justification: The introduction adds Result 4, asserting achievable utility U* + Ω(SReg(T)/T), and explicitly claims that the retained linear upper bound is tight. The main reduction, square-root worst-case rate and mean-based exploitability claim remain; the latter is renumbered from Result 4 to Result 5.

C2.justification: Proposition 3.3 now explicitly limits the worst-case tightness result to principal policies independent of the agent's current strategy. This applicability qualification was absent from v6's theorem statement, although v7's introductory Result 2 still says 'any strategy.' The broader interpretations and Section 6 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same contextual-bandit pseudocode and underlying algorithm choices. Neither version adds software, data access, hardware, runtime or implementation information; the revised proof construction is described under M1 and T1.

R1.justification: v7 adds Arunachaleswaran et al. (2025), Collina et al. (2024) and Kolumbus et al. (2024), modestly extending discussion of private information, prior-free mechanisms and learning games. Section 3.4 also explicitly relates mean-based exploitation to Deng et al. (2019). The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction reorganizes four highlighted results into five and more explicitly separates worst-case and best-case bounds. There are localized prose edits, a shortened Appendix B.2 and an updated publication footnote. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The same payoff matrices and Algorithm 1 remain. v7 reflows equations and boxed descriptions, changes internal-reference colors and rule styling, and displays the expanded Example 4.1 bounds as bullets. No new empirical tables or figures appear.

improvement.justification: v7 improves rigor through the corrected conditioning and principal-utility calculation in Theorem 3.4, and improves completeness through the added best-case tightness construction. The net gain is limited by consistency problems: introductory Result 2 does not reflect Proposition 3.3's narrower scope, and a new summary inequality in Appendix C.2 omits the +δ term retained in Example 4.1 and the final derivation.
